text: analyse frequencies stops, use GTFShift::get_stop_frequency_hourly, producing, , aggregated counting bus servicing per hour. default, analysis performed next business Wednesday, Portugal. text: Using overline attribute GTFShift::get_route_frequency_hourly might best option GTFS shapes share exactly geometry. cases, overlapping lines might merged correctly, causing inconsistent results, street different frequencies along , despite bus stop differences. known issue stplanr::overline2(), method used network aggregation solved yet. alternative, GTFShift provides method GTFShift::network_overline, allows route aggregation. Given simplified network, identifies segments corresponding route uses aggregate attribute defined parameters. can used aggregate frequencies. One approach network simplification centerlines determination. development project, R packages found suiting purpose. Centerline package feature roadmap. Currently, available solutions Python ArcGis. title: 3. Aggregate GTFS feeds
text: Public transit analysis takes advantage standardized GTFS format. However, provision operator makes difficult network aggregated analysis, considering connectivity multimodality. GTFShift::unify proposes simple solution problem, generating aggregated GTFS file given several instances . article uses GTFS feeds library GTFS database Portugal example. Refer vignette(“download”) details.
code: # Get GTFS from library GTFS database for Portugal data = read.csv(system.file("extdata", "gtfs_sources_pt.csv", package = "GTFShift"))  gtfs_list = lapply(c("barreiro", "fertagus"), function(ID) {   feed = GTFShift::load_feed(data$URL[data$ID == ID], create_transfers=FALSE)   # If some GTFS does not have calendar.txt, but another yes, so we must create it to enable unification   if (! ("calendar" %in% names(feed))) feed$calendar = GTFShift::create_calendar(feed)   summary(feed)   return(feed) }) #> tidygtfs object #> files        agency, routes, stop_times, trips, shapes, calendar, calendar_dates, feed_info, stops #> agency       Transportes Colectivos do Barreiro #> service      from 2024-12-01 to 2025-12-31 #> uses         stop_times (no frequencies) #> # routes       20 #> # trips      3029 #> # stop_ids    279 #> # stop_names  162 #> # shapes       75 #> tidygtfs object #> files        agency, routes, stop_times, trips, fare_attributes, fare_rules, shapes, vehicles, calendar, calendar_dates, feed_info, stops #> agency       Fertagus #> service      from 2025-06-03 to 2025-12-03 #> uses         stop_times (no frequencies) #> # routes       3 #> # trips      260 #> # stop_ids    14 #> # stop_names  14 #> # shapes       6

title: 3. Aggregate GTFS feeds
text: unification performed GTFShift::unify(), producing single GTFS instance, saved ZIP file. Option create_transfers enables generation transfers.txt, aggregating close stops, even different GTFS. can displayed using mapview.
code: # Perform unification gtfs_united = GTFShift::unify(gtfs_list[[1]], gtfs_list[[2]], create_transfers = TRUE)  summary(gtfs_united) #> tidygtfs object #> files        agency, routes, stop_times, trips, fare_attributes, fare_rules, shapes, transfers, ., calendar, calendar_dates, feed_info, stops #> agencies     Transportes Colectivos do Barreiro, Fertagus #> service      from 2024-12-01 to 2025-12-31 #> uses         stop_times (no frequencies) #> # routes       23 #> # trips      3289 #> # stop_ids    293 #> # stop_names  176 #> # shapes       81  summary(gtfs_united$transfers) #>  from_stop_id        to_stop_id        transfer_type min_transfer_time #>  Length:1150        Length:1150        Min.   :2     Min.   :120       #>  Class :character   Class :character   1st Qu.:2     1st Qu.:120       #>  Mode  :character   Mode  :character   Median :2     Median :248       #>                                        Mean   :2     Mean   :245       #>                                        3rd Qu.:2     3rd Qu.:350       #>                                        Max.   :2     Max.   :416

title: 3. Aggregate GTFS feeds
code: shape_agency = gtfs_united$trips |>   left_join(gtfs_united$routes, by = "route_id") |>   left_join(gtfs_united$agency, by = "agency_id") |>   select(shape_id, agency_id, agency_name) |>   distinct()  shapes_sf = tidytransit::shapes_as_sf(gtfs_united$shapes) |>   left_join(shape_agency, by = "shape_id") |>   filter(!is.na(agency_id)) mapview::mapview(shapes_sf, zcol = "agency_name", legend = TRUE, layer.name="Agency")
